reviews.text: This game is about DWARVES that dig in a mine and there is skeletons and others monsters that want to destroy the mine. Why ? Who send them ? I do not understand the lore... I've seen a lot of youtube videos that talk about the lore of games like "demon souls" etc... And you have to understand that this game is not like that AT ALL. One of the dwarf is a alchemist, another one is some kind of spellcaster, do they know each others ? Maybe they are siblings ? While I was having fun digging the mine and building all kind of stuff that give extra power to my dwarves I was like "maybe the dwarf alchemist and the dwarf spellcaster are siblings... ?". If you want a good game with a lot of characters, powerups, modifiers, replayability... It's perfect for you ! But if you want to dig into the lore, just RUN AWAY.
Played a few runs, loved it! Already can't wait for more content. And dwarfs FTW.

This game is ok. Not bad, not good. Just ok. Reviewed the day after it released into early access. It plays like those Flash games of old, or the sometimes free games you can get for your mobile phone. It's very easy to figure out the best tactic and then it's down to luck if you get the specific heroes, relics and buildings that are the best. There are some minor synergies between units, buildings and items, that gives small damage buffs, but no actual "builds" you can do, no interesting directions to take your tactics; every run is played out the same way. The difference between getting a low or high score is dependant on luck, what units and buildings you get but more importantly what relics. But even if you get everything lined up perfectly, the game still plays the same way, it's just the damage numbers that go up a bit. It's not like say, 'Slay the Spire', where you go with what you have, roll with the punches and come out on top with a janky and weird deck of cards. Or have a really good deck and lose anyway because you get too greedy and take on every challenge you face. No, Hold the Mine is nothing like that, it's more like a casino machine where you can bet if you win or not. Even 'Luck be a Landlord' has way more interesting mechanics than this game. It becomes boring quite fast. At least for adults. It might suit small children who does not yet grasp the abstraction of planning, how to think in more steps than one, who instead calls everything lucky or unlucky. I don't recommend that you waste your time and money on this. I payed for this game, but even if it was free for everyone I would rather do something else than play it. Edited for typos and errors.

It's a strong start. But the game is simply not DEEP enough for it to earn my recommendation in its current state and at its price. $10 for about two hours of content... I came, I saw, I conquered, and now I'm left to find something else to preoccupy me. The premise is nice, who doesn't like a dig-based mechanic and character pulls? But the more you CHIP AWAY at the content, the quicker you realize there's not much to it. After UNEARTHING the endless mode, you'll quickly own every relic/ tower/ skill and grow bored. There is no story, no variance in gameplay, no exploration, and hardly a difference in the mobs. As much as I wanted this to be a DIAMOND IN THE ROUGH, it's just another unfinished indie game.

目前来看存在很多问题。 1.没有局外成长，局内获取的有限资源让游戏体验很依赖。比如炸蛋怪出现的第一天，没有足够的运气就只能像给无能的丈夫一样看着他进门。 2.人物之间的联动性不高，建筑物、遗物和宝石也不多，后两者的获取难度也有一点点高。我尝试玩了很多局毒咒流和奴役流，非常非常非常容易死在前期。只有龙骑士和狂暴战士的火流能较为稳定的过渡到中期。不过也可能是我比较菜不会规划。 3.现在游戏不能保存，这一点我感觉问题是比较大的。虽然每一局的时间大概只有30分钟左右，但保存机制还是很有必要的。 4.目前无尽模式的难度，哪怕是玩简单模式想要坚持过25天也很困难，尤其是飞天幽灵，血量厚速度快。目前除了铁毡和交两个时停以外我想不出其他能称得上较为简单的击杀方法。 5.对于想做全成就的玩家来说，击杀10个宝箱怪的任务很不友好。这一点我是真破防了，刷了10个小时只杀了3只宝箱怪，这给爆率真是绝了。而且还有bug，有一局中加上无尽模式里击杀的宝箱怪有3只，蛋任务进度条只统计了1只。今天也打了3个小时左右，更是只见到了一只宝箱怪。平心而论如果没有这个任务，就目前游戏的体量，我是完全不会玩这么久的。不客气地说，这很恶心。我想我最近都不会再打开这个游戏了。它实在浪费了，是的就是，浪费了我太多时间。 游戏作为一款独立的小游戏底子不错，如果让我再选一次我依旧愿意为此买单。但现在来看欠缺得还很多，我并不会推荐给其他人。期待后续更新。

2天玩了20个小时，总体评价不错，浅谈下我的意见，希望以后有改进。 1.材料互兑系统，就是黄金可以按比例换宝石。 2.建筑物拆除系统（可以有代价拆除，花钻石等），有时候有好图纸，迟迟没有建筑物的位置 3.按住SHIFT可以快速移动画面切换功能，现在太慢了。 4.开发多些拾取道具，比如定向炸弹或者定向开视野功能。 5.养成系统 6.存档功能 7.宝石3合1升级功能，宝石别涨价。宝石增孔养成 8.后期商店太少，ROLL币太难获得，我有了存钱罐+建筑物给钱后，身上800G没有ROLL币，无法购物，比如可以在山洞里偶遇商店 9.全局可以给一次失败回溯功能（回到开局初，重新抉择一次），以便调整站位和宝石，有时候开局拿到灯，结果暴毙 10.主动技能系统太拉跨，基本没人选，考虑下怎么改进 11.英雄替换系统，后期可替换1个英雄 就写这么多，4月份新版本出来后，我还会提意见，大家觉得我说得不错，点点赞，让开发者看到一个真实喜欢这个游戏人的意见。

A really promising project! Gameplay is simple, split between an addictive resource gathering phase and a tense auto-battler / defence phase. Whether you succeed or fail, you make progress in a rogue-lite skill tree that improves your future runs. Though the game is already fun and addictive, it has a few rough edges, but it also has a ton of room to grow into something much greater. The dev is actively updating and has plans for a ton of new content and something called "Conquest mode", which sounds like it will turn the game into something even more satisfying. Big recommend!

It's a loop that's been done in other games, mine-fight-repeat. but feels really satisfying here. 11 hours in, still unlocking stuff regularly, and every run feels fresh because there are a lot of build options between heroes/hero powers/relics and many of them seem viable. Some games, you just stick to what works if you want to make progress, but with Hold the Mine, I don't feel restricted because it's designed to encourage synergies. My two minor suggestions for the dev: 1) The run summary screen says the number of quests completed, but not which ones, and the quest screen from the main menu doesn't show any ! icons to identify new clears, so I'm just guessing at what I just did. My dude, I smoke a lot of weed, please don't try to make me deduce or remember things. 2) Would appreciate having the leader boards divided by difficulty. I have no interest in playing the impossible difficulty, but would be curious to know how I'm doing against other players at my skill level in medium. So. both very minor issues. And the game is still in Early Access and every update seems to add more and more content, so props to the dev. Great game to lock in and zone out, and weirdly cozy for the subject matter. 5/5

You know when you try a game... and it just falls perfectly into place. It's this game. Mine down the mountain + put characters to defend the gate in an auto battler. It's perfectly executed. You just get one simple game. Maybe not as simple as it looks, might die a few times. :p It took me one weekend to master a few heroes and survive. I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Hold the Mine uses the tried-and-tested mine - upgrade - defend formula (like Dome Keeper), and it does it very well. The gameplay loop is satisfying, progression rewarding, it's easy to do "just one more run" My main wish is for some form of meaningful, tangible meta-progression beyond individual runs. I'd love to see an overworld map where you can expand and upgrade your kingdom, send dwarves on expeditions to new biomes, encounter different enemies, and make decisions that affect the wider world. Perhaps neighboring kingdoms could become allies or rivals, helping or hindering your progress based on your choices. Maybe an idea for Hold the mine 2 hahah The foundation is good. It just feels like there's room for additional layer of long-term progression that could make the game even more compelling
